learn.title: Logging design: workspaces, diagnostic settings and log routing
objectives: Recommend a Log Analytics workspace design (number, region, access mode) that meets residency, security and cost needs
Choose table plans and retention (interactive vs long-term) to balance query needs, compliance and cost
Recommend Azure Monitor Agent with data collection rules for VM, Arc-enabled and custom log collection
Use diagnostic settings and the activity log to route platform logs to Log Analytics, Storage, Event Hubs or partner solutions
Design log delivery to Microsoft Sentinel or a third-party SIEM, including cross-subscription and cross-tenant scenarios
concepts: Log Analytics workspace
The store for Azure Monitor Logs and Microsoft Sentinel; data is held in the workspace region and queried with KQL.
Access control mode
Workspace setting that allows workspace-context access only, or resource-context access where Azure RBAC on a resource grants access to that resource's logs.
Table plans
Analytics (full KQL, alerts, interactive analysis), Basic (cheaper ingestion, 30-day interactive retention, pay per GB scanned) and Auxiliary (lowest ingestion cost for low-touch, high-volume data).
Interactive vs long-term retention
Interactive retention keeps data queryable (up to two years for Analytics); long-term retention keeps it at low cost for up to 12 years, accessed by search jobs or restore.
Azure Monitor Agent (AMA)
The current agent for guest OS data on Azure VMs and Azure Arc-enabled servers; the Log Analytics agent (MMA) was retired in August 2024.
Data collection rule (DCR)
Defines what AMA or the Logs ingestion API collects, optional KQL transformations, and destinations; associated to machines via DCR associations.
Ingestion-time transformation
KQL in a DCR that filters rows, removes or masks columns, or splits data before it is stored, reducing cost and protecting sensitive data.
Diagnostic setting
Per-resource configuration that sends resource logs and platform metrics to Log Analytics, Storage, Event Hubs or a partner solution; up to five per resource.
Activity log
Subscription-level control-plane events kept for 90 days by the platform; a diagnostic setting routes it elsewhere for longer retention.
Event Hubs
Streaming destination used to feed third-party SIEMs and analytics tools; must be in the same region as a regional resource.
Microsoft Sentinel
Cloud-native SIEM enabled on a Log Analytics workspace, ingesting through data connectors.
Azure Lighthouse
Delegated resource management that lets a managing tenant query and configure logging across customer tenants.
comparisons: Log Analytics vs Storage vs Event Hubs
Log Analytics for querying and alerting, Storage for cheap long-term or immutable archive, Event Hubs for streaming to external tools and SIEMs.
Analytics for data you alert on and query often; Basic for high-volume troubleshooting data queried occasionally; Auxiliary for rarely queried audit or verbose data at the lowest ingestion cost.

Start with one workspace; add more for data residency, separate tenants, or to keep high-volume operational data out of Sentinel billing. Use resource-context access rather than extra workspaces for team isolation.
A search job runs one query over long-term data and writes results to a new table; restore brings a time range back for repeated interactive analysis.
AMA with DCR vs diagnostic settings
AMA collects guest OS data (events, syslog, text logs) from machines; diagnostic settings route platform resource logs and metrics from Azure resources.
A commitment tier discounts one workspace's steady daily ingestion; a dedicated cluster pools commitment across workspaces in a region and enables customer-managed keys.
traps: Resource logs are not collected until you create a diagnostic setting; the activity log is collected automatically but kept only 90 days.
Storage accounts and event hubs used by diagnostic settings must be in the same region as a regional resource; the Log Analytics workspace can be in any region.
Analytics interactive retention tops out at two years; longer compliance retention uses long-term retention (up to 12 years) or Storage.
Do not design with the Log Analytics agent (MMA) or the HTTP Data Collector API; use AMA and the Logs ingestion API with DCRs.
When Sentinel is enabled, billable data in that workspace is charged at Sentinel rates, so high-volume operational data may belong in a separate workspace.
Customer-managed keys for Log Analytics require a dedicated cluster.
revision: Default to one workspace per region that has residency rules, with resource-context access for app teams.
Use Azure Policy DeployIfNotExists to enforce diagnostic settings and AMA plus DCR associations at scale.
Use DCR transformations and XPath or syslog filters to cut ingestion volume and strip sensitive columns.
Pick Basic or Auxiliary for noisy data, Analytics for data that drives alerts and Sentinel analytics rules.
Route to Event Hubs for Splunk or QRadar, to partner solutions for Datadog or Elastic, and to Sentinel for an Azure-native SIEM.
Use immutable Blob Storage for WORM compliance archives and lifecycle management for cheap tiers.
Use Azure Lighthouse to manage logging across customer tenants; diagnostic settings can target another tenant's workspace only through Lighthouse.
Use Azure Monitor Private Link Scope with data collection endpoints for private ingestion.

questions.q: Auditors require resource logs to be kept for seven years. The logs are almost never read and do not need KQL queries. You need to minimise cost. Which destination should you recommend?

questions.q: Several application teams share one Log Analytics workspace. Each team must see only logs from the Azure resources it already has access to. You need to minimise administrative effort. What should you recommend?

questions.dom: Design identity, governance, and monitoring solutions
questions.q: Security logs must be retained for seven years in one place. Data older than two years is needed only for occasional investigations. You need to minimise cost and administrative effort. What should you recommend?
